account: Today I read the updated appointment book and kept morning office hours. The secretary reported no new correspondence or news. I have now arrived at the east-bank mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, but nobody has yet answered my request to see the stores. The unusual thread is activity involving bread, the bakery, and the inn. The secretary's notes record reports from Townsfolk 18 and 28 of the baker carrying bread at the inn, and her own sighting of the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread yesterday afternoon. The innkeeper has arranged an eighteen o'clock great-hall presentation today involving local baking, hospitality, and tradespeople; he says I need make no preparations. I suspect the bread activity may be preparation for that presentation, perhaps a community gathering, but I have not seen the preparations or established anything beyond the stated purpose. Townsfolk Two has also repeated 'bridge or port change at bakery,' including near me this morning. The neighbour previously traced that rumour to wheat being carried and bakery lights, not to an actual explained project. I have no reliable evidence of a bridge or port development. Separately, the treasury holds a reported 128 emeralds, but its ledger and obligations remain unknown; there is no evidence connecting that accounting gap to the hospitality activity.
